title: Composition with a Radical and Its Restricted Domain
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let $f(x)=x^{2}$ and $h(x)=\sqrt{x-2}$. Simplify the composite $(f\circ h)(x)$ and state its natural domain.

steps.title: Record the Domain of the Inner Function
steps.explanation: The square root only makes sense for $x-2\\ge 0$, so $h$ itself demands $x\\in[2,\\infty)$.
steps.why: A composite cannot accept any input that its inner function rejects.

steps.title: Apply the Outer Function
steps.explanation: Squaring the output of $h$ cancels the square root, leaving $x-2$ for every $x\\ge 2$.

steps.title: State the Domain of the Composite
steps.explanation: Even though the simplified expression $x-2$ is a polynomial defined everywhere, the composite inherits the restriction $x\\ge 2$ from $h$.
steps.why: The domain of $f\circ h$ is the set of inputs where the evaluation chain actually runs, not the domain of the simplified formula.
